deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page asks what corresponds to the one-parameter case when several linear transformations are given, for instance when the coefficients of a binary form are transformed linearly by the substitution induced from a transformation of the variables. A first attempt there, working with value systems on which all invariants vanish, is struck out. This page restarts the answer.

(1) Group as stabilizer of its invariants. Suppose the invariants J_1, J_2, J_3, ... (polynomials in x = (x_1..x_n)) of the transformation group are known. For an unknown matrix A = (alpha_ik), require J_s(A x) - J_s(x) = 0 identically in x, for every s. Comparing coefficients of the monomials in x gives a system of polynomial relations among alpha_11..alpha_nn. Modern form: G = {A in GL_n : J_s∘A = J_s for all s}, a linear algebraic group defined by these equations.

(2) Local parametrization near the identity. Expand the solutions in power series in parameters p_1, p_2, ...:
  alpha_ik = delta_ik + l_ik(p_1,...) + (terms of order >= 2, e.g. c_ik p_1 p_2 + ...).
Here l_ik is linear in the p's. Hilbert writes 'm' for the Kronecker delta: m = 0 for i != k, m = 1 for i = k.

(3) Infinitesimal generators. If m linearly independent parameters remain, the linear parts give m linear (infinitesimal) transformations x_i' = x_i + p_r sum_k l_ik^{(r)} x_k, for r = 1..m. In modern terms these are a basis X_1..X_m of the Lie algebra g = Lie(G), with dim G = m. My gloss: the infinitesimal invariance conditions are sum_{i,k} l_ik^{(r)} x_k dJ_s/dx_i = 0.

(4) Recovering the finite group. 'From these the general transformation with arbitrary parameters must result by infinitely repeated application.' This is Lie's principle: the finite transformations are generated by the one-parameter subgroups exp(t X_r), i.e. A = lim (I + X/N)^N = exp(X).

(5) The converse problem is named but left unanswered: the condition for a given system of linear transformations to be of this kind. The sentence is incomplete. The intended answer (mine) is closure of the span of the X_r under commutators, i.e. Lie's group conditions.

(6) Programme for the invariants. Look for an invariant that is linear in the x' and also contains the parameters p, and is unchanged when the p are simultaneously suitably transformed. The model is the linear form u·x with u transforming contragrediently, giving a 'universal' linear covariant. From this linear invariant one should 'easily' form all invariants and recognize their finiteness. This is a plan, not a derivation, and no proof is given.

The page thus outlines how to reduce invariant theory, including finiteness, for an arbitrary continuous linear group (a Lie group in the sense of Lie) to infinitesimal data.
errors: Notational clash: 'm' denotes both the Kronecker delta in alpha_ik = m + l_ik + ... and the number of independent parameters.
The higher-order terms are written schematically as 'p_1 p_2 + ...' without coefficients; they should read sum c_ik^{(rs)} p_r p_s + ....

'Unendlich häufige Anwendung' (exponentiating infinitesimal transformations) yields only the identity component of the stabilizer group. The full group {A : J(Ax) = J(x)} can be disconnected, e.g. O(n), or finite groups, which have no infinitesimal transformations at all.

The condition for a system of infinitesimal linear transformations to generate a group is announced but not stated. The sentence 'Bedingung dafür, dass umgekehrt ein System ... von derart ist' is incomplete. The correct condition is closure under brackets (Lie).

The final claim that all invariants and their finiteness follow 'leicht' from a linear invariant with parameters is unjustified. Finite generation fails for some linear (non-reductive) groups (Nagata 1959, counterexample to Hilbert's 14th problem). Maurer's 1899 attempt along infinitesimal lines was erroneous.

Possible circularity: the group is defined via its invariants J_s, yet the goal is to find invariants. This is meaningful only as characterizing the group by a known set of invariants and then studying its full invariant ring, which may be larger than the ring generated by the J_s.

results.what: Defining a linear group as the set of matrices A with J_s(Ax) = J_s(x); the polynomial relations on the alpha_ik obtained by comparing coefficients
results.modern_name: Stabilizer of a set of polynomials as a linear algebraic group
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Clebsch, Gordan, Lie); formalized by Cartan, Chevalley, Borel in the 20th century

results.what: Power-series parametrization near the identity, alpha_ik = delta_ik + l_ik(p) + ..., giving m independent infinitesimal linear transformations
results.modern_name: Lie algebra of a linear group; infinitesimal generators
results.usually_credited_to: Sophus Lie (1870s-1888, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen with Engel)

results.what: Recovering the finite transformations by infinitely repeated application of infinitesimal ones
results.modern_name: Exponential map; one-parameter subgroups generate the identity component

results.what: Programme: obtain all invariants of an arbitrary continuous linear group from a linear invariant with transformed parameters, and prove finiteness
results.modern_name: Finite generation of invariant rings for general linear (Lie/algebraic) groups; precursor of Hilbert's 14th problem; approach via the contragredient linear form u·x and polarization
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's 14th problem (1900); attempted by L. Maurer (1899); settled negatively by Nagata (1959); positively for reductive groups (Hilbert 1890, Weyl, Mumford, Nagata)

deep.surprise_reason: The infinitesimal and Lie-theoretic content is standard Lie theory of the 1880s. Notable is the unpublished evidence that around 1890-91 Hilbert sketched extending finiteness to arbitrary continuous linear groups defined via Lie's infinitesimal transformations, believing it 'leicht'. That claim is false in general (Nagata). This is an early private precursor of the 14th problem and parallels Maurer's 1899 flawed approach, but contains no proof or new theorem.

checkable.asserts: Rotations preserve the invariant J = x1^2 + x2^2: the relation J(Ax) - J(x) = 0 holds.
The parametrized alpha_ik have the form delta_ik + l_ik(p) + higher order, as on the page (alpha_11 = 1 - p^2/2 + ..., alpha_12 = -p + ...).
The finite transformation is recovered by exponentiating (infinitely repeated application of) the infinitesimal generator.
Infinitesimal invariance condition sum l_ik x_k dJ/dx_i = 0 for the generator l = [[0,-1],[1,0]].
The stabilizer contains a reflection (det = -1) that is not a product of exponentials of the Lie algebra, so exponentiation gives only the identity component.
The linear form u·x with parameters u transformed contragrediently is an invariant linear in x, the type of 'lineare Invariante' Hilbert proposes.
Closure of infinitesimal generators under commutators (here sl2): the Lie condition answering Hilbert's unstated 'Bedingung'.
